take_homes: Count how many of the available sources the output actually cites. That is my real uptake number, and I shouldn't tell the board a percentage before I know it.
Before I roll a plan out, ask 'what would make us drop this?'. If I can't answer, it's only a belief.
A multi-agent forum needs each agent to say what it knows and doesn't know, a synthesizer that picks instead of averaging, and a human who decides. The first pass wasn't usable on its own.

monday.move: Take the sales-team setup I built over the weekend and write down which of its claims have a source. Count how many of the available docs it cites, then ask someone in sales what would make them drop it.
monday.who: me, plus one person in sales
monday.when: Monday morning, before building anything new
monday.stop_condition: If the sales person says nobody asked for it and nobody would maintain it, I stop building and don't add more.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering asked for it, and I haven't checked who would maintain it. I may also skip the check, because it looked fine.

misconception.why: I still think good agents give good output, but the module's own line, 'nothing in the room checked it', applied to my work. Access wasn't uptake, and I hadn't been measuring uptake at all. It's shaken, not changed. I skipped the review steps and nothing in the module forced me to do them.

one_line: the first half is stuff my engineers already do, but the room-scale forum and the 'count the folders it cites' idea were new to me, so it's worth it for someone running a whole org.
